title: Gaussian exponential moment identity
statement: For every $t,z\in\mathbb{R}$ with $t\ge0$, the standard Gaussian expectation satisfies $e^{tz^2}=\int_{\mathbb{R}}e^{\sqrt{2t}\,z g}\,dN(0,1)(g)$.
replaced:
For every real $t \ge 0$ and every real $z$,
\[
  e^{t z^2} \;=\; \int e^{\sqrt{2t}\, z\, g}\, \mathrm{d}N(0,1)(g),
\]
i.e.\ $e^{tz^2}$ equals the moment generating function of a standard Gaussian
evaluated at $s = \sqrt{2t}\, z$.
